common_mistakes.mistake: Isp misses the upper STOP position or leaves before Pac has transferred to the landing.
common_mistakes.consequence: The lift resumes its motion and Pac may need another ride to reach the landing safely.
common_mistakes.recovery: Remain on the solid lift and wait for its next upper pass, then reapply STOP.

confidence_reason: Authored source and one ordinary-input route define the lift, pad order, lethal gaps and successful both-exit path. Failure recovery follows source behavior and was not exercised in the retained passing attempt.

confirmed: The subtitle correctly suggested an upward marrow route where the heroes must mind one another.
The screenshot shows distinct Isp STOP and Pac STEADY controls and separate exits.
The first pass correctly treated recovery and input reliability as unknown from idle frames.
missed_mechanics: The moving lift carries both heroes upward on an 8-second cycle; Isp STOP freezes it for the transfer and opens Pac landing.
Pac STEADY stabilizes the bridge and opens Isp’s crossing. Isp RESCUE latches, stabilizes the bridge permanently, and opens Pac’s finish gate.
Both slime regions are lethal and lie beneath mandatory lift/bridge segments.
The actual “glucose isn’t free” text is flavor; there is no glucose resource or fee.
Two optional role-owned collectibles sit on the lift and landing.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass treated the glucose line as a possible resource/access warning. Source mechanics show it is not a gate or timed resource.
The first-pass prior ledger attributed Isp STOP and Pac RESCUE to level_04; actual earlier source and screenshot show Pac STEADY and Isp RESCUE.
changed_judgments: Reasoning stays at 3: the multi-step sequence confirms the first-pass suspicion that elevator access and pads interact, but source makes the actual causal order explicit.
Cooperation changes from 3 to 4 because Isp/Pac/Isp perform successive necessary pad roles, and each opens/stabilizes the other route.
Execution rises from 2 to 3 because both heroes must transfer from a moving lift to raised surfaces and cross a narrow unstable bridge.
Timing changes from null to 2: the lift has a repeatable 8-second travel cycle and a useful upper stop point; the route has a broad repeatable opportunity.
Hazards changes from null to 2 because slime is beneath mandatory lift/bridge segments; the surfaces provide a safe route but a fall is lethal.
Novelty rises from 2 to 3 because earlier ferry and bridge lessons are recombined in a vertical lift-and-gate sequence.
Recovery cost changes from null to 2 because missing the lift cycle repeats travel, and a bridge fall can reset the room from the beginning.
Solution clarity changes from 3 to 2: visible pad cues orient the route and the hint states the order, though the base screenshot does not spell out cross-gate effects.
unresolved: No failed ordinary route directly measures bridge-fall frequency or actual player recovery behavior; the recovery estimate follows source reset mechanics.
Scripted success does not establish that first-time pairs discover the lift stop and pad sequence.
Human timing, enjoyment, co-op communication and perceived fairness remain unmeasured.

single_operator_note: One operator must switch among the two key groups and time movement from a moving lift while the other hero occupies a pad; simultaneous two-character attention is substantially greater here than in a route with only sequential latches. This note is outside the two-human baseline scores.
